page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-32 is a memory-optimized server instance featuring 32 vCPUs and 256 GB of RAM, yielding a ratio of 8 GB of memory per core. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor with 16 physical cores and 2 threads per core, it utilizes dedicated CPU allocation. The processor architecture includes 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8) for accelerated mathematical and matrix operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong performance in memory bandwidth, reaching 208.51 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 99.59 GB/sec for large-block write operations. It also shows strong results in Geekbench image processing and text processing, alongside a static web serving throughput of 44.59 GB/sec. Most other compute benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core (15821.0) and Passmark CPU (38513.51), fall within the average range. Tradeoffs include the complete absence of local storage and GPU hardware, as well as zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. It is configured for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching, text and image processing pipelines, and medium-scale language model prompt processing.
